fr.recommendations:
• Post a clearly visible address number at the street-facing driveway entrance so responders can confirm the correct property from the road.
• Mark or label the secondary access point so responders arriving from an unfamiliar direction can quickly locate it.
• Trim vegetation along both sides of the access drive so emergency vehicles can pass without obstruction.
• Cut back dense vegetation near the detached structure to keep a clear path for responders approaching that building on foot.
• Keep all gates in fenced sections unlocked or secured with a knox box so responders are not delayed gaining entry.
• Mark which gate or fenced opening provides the most direct route to the main residence.
• Clear the walkway of any overhanging vegetation so responders can move quickly between the main residence and the detached structure.
• Keep the vehicle parking area clear enough that an emergency vehicle can turn around or reposition without being blocked.
• Post the location of the solar panel system's emergency shutoff in a visible location near the main electrical panel or primary entry point so responders can de-energize the system quickly.
• Identify and mark any roof sections covered by solar panels on or near the main breaker panel to alert responders before roof access or ventilation operations.
• Keep the open lawn area free of parked vehicles or stored equipment so it remains available as a staging area for responders.

wildfire.recommendations:
• Thin trees within the scattered clusters closest to the structures to reduce the amount of vegetation feeding a fire.
• Remove shrubs growing directly against or within a few feet of any structure walls or corners.
• Keep the open ground between scattered trees and structures clear of dead leaves, fallen branches, and loose plant debris.
• Trim lower branches on trees near structures so flames cannot climb from ground vegetation up into the tree canopy.
• Clear dead or dry material from beneath any tree clusters located close to structures.
• Maintain the existing open areas between vegetation and structures by preventing shrubs or small trees from establishing in those gaps.
